name: Bioluminescent Subdermal Array
description: Introduces genes from Aequorea victoria jellyfish and deep-sea anglerfish to produce bioluminescent protein chains beneath the skin. The result is a soft, controllable glow that can be patterned, dimmed, or brightened at will. Popular installations include glowing circuit-trace patterns along the arms, luminous freckles, and full-body constellations. The light is real — it illuminates a dark room. High-tier versions from Lacuna Genomics allow programmable patterns that shift throughout the day. Street versions from backroom gene clinics are often stuck on a single color and brightness, turning the user into a permanent lantern. In the Narrows, people with glowskin are walking nightlights, and some lease their presence to vendors who can't afford electric signage.
procedure: Subdermal injection matrix with retroviral carrier, single session
expression_time: 2–3 weeks; glow intensifies over first 6 months
reversibility: Reversible with targeted gene silencing; leaves faint scarring along injection matrix lines
side_effects: Persistent low-level glow during sleep (cannot fully extinguish)
Budget versions occasionally produce UV-range light that causes sunburn to nearby skin
social_perception: Celebrated in nightlife culture. Tier 1 laborers with stuck-on glowskin are sometimes exploited as living light sources. Corporate environments consider it unprofessional except during social events.
story_hooks: A murder victim's glowskin recorded the moment of death — the stress-triggered luminescence pattern is frozen into the skin like a photograph
A glowskin user discovers their pattern matches a proprietary Lacuna Genomics sequence they never paid for — someone pirated the gene package into their installation
